analysis.title: The next big tech rotation? Even 55% earnings growth may not save tech from what's coming
key_insights: Deutsche Bank is turning tactically cautious on mega-cap growth and tech, arguing the latest rotation into the sector is approaching exhaustion.

DB sees about 4 percentage points of relative upside left for mega-cap growth and tech before the upper end of the long-term trend channel, versus about 16 points of downside if earlier rotation patterns repeat.
This is the fifth major rotation into tech in two years, and prior reversals have tended to be sharp, inverted V-shaped moves.
DB tracks four major rotations out of mega-cap growth and tech since July 2024. Relative underperformance in those episodes ranged from 17.5 to 18.4 percentage points.

In those four episodes tech fell a median 14.8% while the rest of the market gained a median 3%. The broader S&P 500 still declined in all four, so a rotation out of tech does not imply a rising market.
Investors have started reducing exposure to mega-cap growth and tech, but positioning remains overweight versus the rest of the market. Most other sectors sit near neutral or underweight.
A gradual reallocation from tech into underowned sectors could be enough to drive large relative underperformance without aggressive outright selling.
DB expects mega-cap growth and tech earnings to grow about 55% y/y in Q3, but argues this may not sustain near-term outperformance because investors question future profitability.
DB expects about 21% earnings growth outside tech, stronger than the market appears to appreciate, and the bar for the rest of the market is lower.
The S&P 500 equal-weight index relative to the Nasdaq 100 (RSP/NDX) is bouncing off the lower end of its long-term trend channel, an early sign of a possible reversal.
NDX has traded well bid as rates have surged. The note asks whether a pause in rates could let tech start underperforming (RSP/NDX ratio vs the US 10-year yield).
Tech is roughly 40% of US market cap and 30% of Asia, versus about 9% in Europe. DB sees Europe as better positioned for a rotation away from tech while staying structurally constructive on tech.

The cost of AI has roughly halved every quarter on a like-for-like basis over three years (Epoch data). Bottlenecks shift to electricity, land, grid connections, physical infrastructure and regulatory approvals.
DB argues proprietary data, regulatory licenses, sticky customer relationships and scarce physical assets could become more valuable as AI gets cheaper.

sector_views.rationale: DB is tactically cautious: about 4 points of relative upside versus 16 points of downside, with positioning still overweight. It stays structurally constructive.
Expected earnings growth of about 21% against a lower bar, and positioning is neutral to underweight, leaving room for catch-up.
Tech is only about 9% of European market cap, so the region has the least exposure to a rotation away from tech.

earnings_insights: DB expects mega-cap growth and tech Q3 earnings growth of roughly 55% y/y (DB estimate, not yet reported).
DB expects roughly 21% earnings growth y/y outside tech in Q3 (DB estimate, not yet reported).

trade_ideas.description: Relative-value rotation: favor the rest of the S&P 500 (equal-weight, RSP) over the Nasdaq 100 (NDX), and European equities over US tech-heavy indices
trade_ideas.rationale: Asymmetric tactical risk/reward in tech (4 points of upside vs 16 of downside) and underowned non-tech sectors.
trade_ideas.risk: A broader market decline: the S&P 500 fell in all four prior rotations out of tech.

risk_factors: Rotation out of tech may not mean a rising market, as the S&P 500 declined in all four prior episodes.
Rising rates have so far supported NDX.
Investors may keep rewarding tech earnings growth, which DB itself expects at about 55% y/y in Q3.
Positioning is still overweight tech, so the rotation could be gradual rather than sharp.

tension_points.bull_case: Mega-cap growth and tech earnings are expected to grow about 55% y/y in Q3, NDX has traded well bid as rates surged, and DB stays structurally constructive on tech.
tension_points.bear_case: The latest rotation into tech is near exhaustion, with about 4 points of relative upside versus 16 points of downside, and positioning is still overweight. Even 55% growth may not sustain outperformance as investors question future profitability.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A pause in rates that lets tech underperform would support the bear case. For the rotation call, RSP/NDX failing to hold the lower end of its trend channel would invalidate it.
